topics.label: Pipeline as Code
topics.desc: Declaring CI/CD workflows in version-controlled YAML/DSL so pipelines are reviewable, reproducible, and evolve with the codebase.

topics.label: Continuous Integration
topics.desc: Frequently merging to a shared mainline with automated build and test on every change to catch integration defects early.

topics.label: Continuous Delivery
topics.desc: Keeping every validated build releasable at all times, with promotion to production gated by a manual or automated decision.

topics.label: Stages & Gates
topics.desc: Structuring a pipeline into sequential stages with quality gates that block promotion when tests, scans, or approvals fail.

topics.label: Runners & Agents
topics.desc: Ephemeral or persistent worker machines that execute pipeline jobs, often autoscaled and isolated per build for reproducibility.

topics.label: Triggers & Webhooks
topics.desc: Event sources (push, PR, tag, schedule, manual) that start pipelines, typically via SCM webhooks or polling.

topics.label: Matrix & Parallel Builds
topics.desc: Fanning a job across combinations of OS, runtime, and config to test the build product matrix concurrently.

topics.label: Build Dependency Graph
topics.desc: Modeling compilation as a DAG of targets and inputs so the build tool rebuilds only what transitively changed.

topics.label: Incremental & Cached Builds
topics.desc: Reusing prior outputs keyed by input hashes to skip unchanged work, the core lever for fast feedback at scale.

topics.label: Dependency Resolution
topics.desc: Computing a consistent set of transitive package versions satisfying declared constraints, often an NP-hard SAT problem.

topics.label: Lockfiles & Pinning
topics.desc: Recording exact resolved versions and hashes so installs are deterministic and reproducible across machines and time.

topics.label: Semantic Versioning
topics.desc: MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH contract communicating breaking, additive, and fix changes to enable safe automated dependency ranges.

topics.label: Hermetic Builds
topics.desc: Sandboxing builds from network and host state so outputs depend only on declared inputs, enabling reproducible artifacts.

topics.label: Monorepo Build Tooling
topics.desc: Tools like Bazel/Nx that track fine-grained targets across a single large repo to build and test only affected projects.

topics.label: Container Fundamentals
topics.desc: OS-level virtualization isolating processes via namespaces and cgroups, sharing the host kernel for lightweight portability.

topics.label: OCI Image Format
topics.desc: Standard layered image spec of content-addressed tarballs plus a manifest, enabling portable, dedupable container artifacts.

topics.label: Image Build Files
topics.desc: Declarative recipes (Dockerfile) whose ordered instructions each produce a cacheable layer that composes the final image.

topics.label: Layer Caching & Optimization
topics.desc: Ordering instructions and minimizing layers so unchanged steps hit the cache, shrinking build time and image size.

topics.label: Multi-Stage Builds
topics.desc: Using throwaway build stages to compile, then copying only artifacts into a slim runtime image free of toolchains.

topics.label: Image Registries
topics.desc: Services storing and distributing OCI images by tag and digest, the distribution hub between build and orchestration.

topics.label: Container Runtimes
topics.desc: Low-level engines (runc, containerd, CRI-O) that unpack images and launch isolated processes per the OCI runtime spec.

topics.label: Image Scanning & Hardening
topics.desc: Scanning layers for CVEs and minimizing attack surface via distroless/non-root images to reduce runtime exposure.

topics.label: Orchestration Fundamentals
topics.desc: Scheduling containers across a cluster while maintaining desired state, health, and placement for resilient services.

topics.label: Kubernetes Architecture
topics.desc: Control plane (API server, etcd, scheduler, controllers) plus node kubelets reconciling declared state via a watch loop.

topics.label: Pods & Workload Controllers
topics.desc: Pods as the schedulable unit, managed by Deployments, StatefulSets, and DaemonSets that own replica lifecycle and rollout.

topics.label: Service & Ingress Networking
topics.desc: Stable virtual IPs, DNS, and L7 ingress routing pod-to-pod and external traffic across an ephemeral cluster network.

topics.label: Scheduling & Affinity
topics.desc: Placing pods onto nodes using resource requests, taints/tolerations, and affinity rules to honor capacity and topology.

topics.label: Autoscaling
topics.desc: Horizontal pod, vertical pod, and cluster autoscalers that adjust replicas and nodes to match load and resource pressure.

topics.label: Operators & CRDs
topics.desc: Custom controllers encoding operational knowledge to manage stateful apps via custom resources, extending the K8s API.

topics.label: Service Mesh
topics.desc: Sidecar-proxy layer (Istio, Linkerd) providing mTLS, traffic shaping, and telemetry without changing application code.

topics.label: IaC Fundamentals
topics.desc: Defining infrastructure as version-controlled code so environments are reproducible, reviewable, and auditable.

topics.label: Declarative vs Imperative
topics.desc: Specifying desired end-state and letting the tool compute changes, versus scripting explicit provisioning steps.

topics.label: State Management
topics.desc: Tracking real-world resources in a state file so the tool can diff, plan, and reconcile against declared configuration.

topics.label: Plan & Apply Workflow
topics.desc: Previewing the diff between desired and actual state before applying, the safety mechanism of Terraform-style tooling.

topics.label: Modules & Reuse
topics.desc: Parameterized, composable infrastructure components that encapsulate patterns and enforce consistency across stacks.

topics.label: Drift Detection
topics.desc: Detecting divergence between declared state and live infrastructure caused by manual changes, then reconciling it.

topics.label: Immutable Infrastructure
topics.desc: Replacing servers with new prebaked images rather than mutating them in place, eliminating configuration drift.

topics.label: Config Externalization
topics.desc: Separating configuration from code per twelve-factor so one artifact runs across environments via injected settings.

topics.label: Secrets Management
topics.desc: Centrally storing, access-controlling, and auditing credentials in vaults instead of source, the baseline of operational security.

topics.label: Secret Rotation & Leasing
topics.desc: Issuing short-lived, automatically rotated or dynamic credentials to shrink the blast radius of any leak.

topics.label: Configuration Management Tools
topics.desc: Agents like Ansible/Chef/Puppet that converge host state to a declared baseline idempotently across fleets.

topics.label: Feature Flags
topics.desc: Runtime toggles decoupling deploy from release, enabling gradual rollout, kill switches, and experimentation.

topics.label: Environment Promotion
topics.desc: Moving the same artifact through dev/staging/prod with environment-specific config to ensure parity and reduce surprises.

topics.label: Runtime Secret Injection
topics.desc: Delivering secrets to workloads at runtime via mounted volumes, sidecars, or env vars rather than baking them into images.

topics.label: Deployment Fundamentals
topics.desc: Mechanics of safely shipping a new version to running infrastructure while controlling downtime and risk.

topics.label: Blue-Green Deployment
topics.desc: Running two identical environments and switching traffic atomically, enabling instant cutover and rollback.

topics.label: Canary Releases
topics.desc: Routing a small traffic slice to a new version and watching metrics before progressively widening exposure.

topics.label: Rolling Deployment
topics.desc: Replacing instances incrementally so capacity stays up, the default low-cost strategy for stateless services.

topics.label: Progressive Delivery
topics.desc: Automating canary analysis and rollout decisions on live SLO signals to advance or abort releases hands-free.

topics.label: Rollback & Recovery
topics.desc: Reverting quickly to a known-good version, the essential safety net that makes aggressive deployment cadence viable.

topics.label: GitOps
topics.desc: Treating a Git repo as the single source of truth, with agents continuously reconciling cluster state to it.

topics.label: Zero-Downtime Deploys
topics.desc: Coordinating connection draining, health checks, and backward-compatible changes so users see no interruption.

topics.label: Artifact Repositories
topics.desc: Versioned stores (Artifactory, Nexus, package registries) holding immutable build outputs as the source for deploys.

topics.label: Release Versioning
topics.desc: Conventions tying built artifacts to commits and tags so any running version is traceable to its exact source.

topics.label: Artifact Promotion
topics.desc: Promoting one immutable, tested artifact across environments instead of rebuilding, guaranteeing what was tested ships.

topics.label: SBOM & Provenance
topics.desc: Recording an artifact's dependency manifest and verifiable build origin for supply-chain transparency and audit.

topics.label: Artifact Signing
topics.desc: Cryptographically signing artifacts (e.g. Sigstore) so consumers verify integrity and authorship before deployment.

topics.label: Release Automation
topics.desc: Automating changelog, tagging, and publish from commit conventions to make releases repeatable and low-ceremony.

topics.label: Supply Chain Security
topics.desc: Securing the build-to-deploy path against tampering using frameworks like SLSA, attestations, and policy gates.
